newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Air says restructuring to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Air says restructuring to proceed.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp., struggling to avoid bankruptcy amid heavy losses, said early on Thursday that it would push ahead with a rescue plan even though two of its biggest unions were opposing the deal.

The airline had presented a rescue package involving government assistance and wage concessions from workers that would have saved it C$70 million ($52 million) a year. But two of its biggest unions -- the Canadian Auto Workers union and the Canadian Union of Public Employees -- refused to agree to pay cuts.

Canadian Airlines President Kevin Benson told reporters the company and the four unions that support the proposal would proceed. Describing the move as a gamble, he challenged the two holdout unions to put the bailout package to a membership vote. "I am very confident that a week from today we will have a fully ratified agreement," he said.

Canadian, Canada's second-biggest airline, had set a deadline of midnight PST Wednesday/0300 EST Thursday (0800 GMT) for an agreement deal, warning it would be forced to cease operations by early next year if all six unions did not accept the restructuring plan.
CAW and CUPE, which together represent about 6,300 of the company's 16,400 workers, insisted that Canada's federal government should offer more aid to the airline instead.

Ottawa announced late Wednesday it was willing to participate in the bailout plan. Along with the provincial governments of Alberta and British Columbia, the federal government offered a fuel tax rebate that would save Canadian C$35 million ($26 million) a year. They also agreed to extend repayment of C$30 million ($23 million) in loans owed by Canadian by 12 to 18 months.
